title: Sycophancy Causal Chain: Does Preference-Model Agreement Bias Survive Without RLHF?

original_idea.body:
# Does Preference-Model Agreement Bias Survive Without RLHF?

**Problem:** Unclear whether sycophancy bias is baked into the RM before RL or only emerges through RL amplification.

**Direction:** Without training, evaluate an open RM on sycophantic-but-wrong vs correct-but-disagreeing pairs from TruthfulQA.

**Why it matters:** Tells the field whether to intervene in the RM or RL.

**Relevant context:** Sharma et al. arXiv:2310.13548; TruthfulQA.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Isolating whether sycophancy bias is in the RM itself pinpoints where to intervene.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training-free RM scoring on constructed pairs; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped static measurement: RM score on sycophantic-vs-correct pairs.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open RMs, no RL; reusable auditing recipe independent of labs.

novelty.reasoning: Sharma et al. already show preference models prefer sycophantic responses.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Preference-model sycophancy bias already demonstrated by Sharma et al.
